prompt: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art sprite concept for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: a single TENDER enemy of the Iron Tide, a large slow carrier drone seen broadside. A long, wide, flat-bellied hull with a clipped delta silhouette: a blunt wedge nose pointing left, a low armored back ridge with a small sensor fin, and a squared-off stern with two stubby engine nozzles glowing warm orange. Dark gunmetal hull plates with steel-blue top highlights and rust-violet seams, a row of tiny bright green running lights along the flank, each enclosed by a dark outline. The whole underside is a long closed ventral hangar bay: a ribbed segmented bay door with small porthole slots through which three seed-shaped pod drones can be seen hanging nose-down in their racks, lit by a dim magenta interior glow. Heavy, wide, readable silhouette like a flying cargo barge. Broadside side view facing left, the whole craft centered with a generous empty margin on a perfectly flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background. Crisp chunky pixel art with a 1-pixel near-black navy outline at the sprite's native pixel scale, flat saturated fills with three-step shading ramps lit from the top-left, no anti-aliasing, no scenery, no stars, no cast shadow, no glow bleeding onto the background, no text, no labels.
